reviews.verdict: Recommends it even to non-fans; the shared Great House and House-versus-House intrigue is a risk that pays off.
Excellent game of narrative intrigue and action for fans of the books and films; misses random events for dynastic play.
Loves it as a showcase of Powered by the Apocalypse design; great for one-shot mysteries and introducing newcomers.
Top recommendation of the new hardback; a go-to game for learning PbtA and onboarding new players.
Praises the narrative focus and easy Keeper prep; notes very light rules and reliance on genre cliches.

notes: Zatu review covers the earlier edition (2020, no edition named).

reviews.verdict: Strong, engaging lore tour and handy prep tool that every Dungeon Master should own.
Recommended as a coffee-table book with great art; dislikes the Mordenkainen narration and it's not a game volume.
A fun romp through beloved settings for veteran gamers and DMs; weaker on Mystara and Eberron.
A pretty good edition with renewed horror focus; dislikes dropped original clans and heavy in-universe fiction.

notes: No independent reviews found; recently released (about two weeks old).

reviews.verdict: Superb, relaxing and cosy; balances structured rules with creative freedom and may help aspiring writers.
A genuinely lovely cosy solo game, though the layout splits and misplaces rules explanations.
Favourable: a relaxing writing game that could help with writer's block.
Strongly positive: thorough world creation, excellent atmosphere, lovely art and layout, plus a solo variant.
Enthusiastic: a dream for vampire pen-pals, free choice of vampire and world, intuitive system, beautiful book.
